answer: Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the jetty checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. The vertex graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the orchard audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 4 times its size, so a group of 93 keys loses far more than 93 single identities would. That is 33 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
